device: CPU only; CUDA initialization and nvidia-smi failed during the campaign

control.policy: 1 MiB no-admission provider over conventional mmap

operation_shared_rerun.device: CPU only (-ngl 0); GPU visibility was intermittent
operation_shared_rerun.protocol: one long-lived server per policy; request order c4, c1, c2, c8; 16 output tokens; one repetition
caveats: Only one run per policy; timings are directional, not confidence results.
The control and candidate formed different dynamic batches, visible in their different operation totals, so source-byte reduction is not a pure cache-policy effect.
Sixteen generated tokens truncate every function before it compiles; byte-identical response text, not pass count, is the useful quality check here.
The copy-on-admission policy still churned and was 17% to 61% slower across c1, c2, c4, and c8 in this single run.
One sequential campaign per policy is insufficient for confidence intervals.
The candidate ran before the control; page-cache and thermal state were not alternated.
Worker-hit counts include threads sharing the current expert and are not expert-operation hits.
Operation-level telemetry was implemented after this pilot and needs a rebuilt rerun.
No physical-I/O, RSS/PSS, VRAM, board energy, or accepted-code throughput was captured.
The one-answer correctness difference may be batching variation and is not evidence of a quality change.
